utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner for the Prosecution, assisted by Alma Imamovic, our case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to our colleagues from the Prosecution and everyone in and around the courtroom. I am Vasvija Vidovic, and Mr. Nicholas Robson, for the Defence of General Rasim Delic, with our case manager, Lejla Gluhic, and our intern, Lejla Kevat [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just one little housekeeping matter before we call the witness. It's with respect to one of the two motions by the Defence to which the Prosecution responded yesterday. It's going to be an oral decision. The Trial Chamber now delivers its oral decision on the "Defence Motion for an Adjournment of Hearing" filed on 10 March 2008. The Prosecution responded orally on 11 March 2008, indicating that it neither opposes nor supports the motion. The Defence motion requested an adjournment of the trial proceedings scheduled for 1 and 2 April 2008 for the reason that Ms. Vidovic is appearing as lead counsel in another case before the Appeals Chamber. The Defence states that without an adjournment on the requested dates, Ms. Vidovic will not be able to proof the Defence witness who is scheduled to testify on 3rd and 4th April 2008, which would jeopardise the accused's right to have adequate time and facilities for preparation of his defence. The Trial Chamber agrees with the Defence that given the circumstances, it is in the interests of justice to grant an adjournment on the requested dates. As such, the Trial Chamber grants the Defence motion for an adjournment of hearing on the 1st and 2nd of April, 2008. An additional hearing will be held on the 14th of April, 2008, to compensate, in part, for the time lost as a result of this adjournment. Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Could we please ask the Court Usher to bring in Witness Halim Husic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please be brought into court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Husic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Husic, may I just remind you that at the beginning of your testimony, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth, and that, therefore, you are still bound by the declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, before you begin, can I just round out my question of yesterday at the end of the day. Mr. Husic, yesterday, when we disbanded here, I was in the process of asking you a question, and I wanted to refer you to part of your testimony which gave me the impression that your forces were fighting against the HVO forces. It was at a time when you were testifying about a young man, Brkic. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right. And the trial record has your testimony as something like this: "He was a minor, a young boy who joined the group of Ramo Durmis for training. And as they were moving in the area of responsibility under the control of the HVO, they drew fire from them and, among other things, this young boy was killed." Then there was a question saying: "When you say that it was impossible to communicate, what are you referring to?" You said: "I'm referring to the fact that the HVO forces had cut off internally the various parts of the Bila Valley, one from another." Now, that part of the testimony left me with the impression that you were fighting against the HVO; but hardly a page later, still talking about what I thought were the same incidents, you said: "All armed formations that have not placed themselves under the command of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina are to be dealt with straight away. As for the HVO units, full cooperation should be established with them due to there being part of the regular armed forces. Instructions as to the further modes of organisation will soon follow." Now, this part says clearly that you're cooperating with the HVO, hence my question yesterday: Who were you actually fighting against at this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At this time, we were on the defence lines against the Chetniks or the Serbian-Montenegrin aggressor on Vlasic in the Bila Valley, where the 306th Mountain Brigade was and the HVO Brigade Frankopan from Guca Gora, and some other units, groups of armed men that we discussed yesterday, they did not have any mutual conflicts; but in occasional incidents, especially after the HVO forces put up blockades or check-points controlling the movement of anyone, they would occasionally opened fire. These incidents were the one that I actually was referring to that you understood as a conflict between these forces. This minor who was killed did not belong to the 306th Mountain Brigade. He was a young boy who was 15 or 16 at the time, and he was in one of these armed groups of Ramo Durmis, who was training them; and on this occasion, fire was opened on them. Now, this happened above the village Suhi Dol, an area that belonged to the Bosniaks. However, above them were the HVO lines, someone just opened fire willfully and murdered, killed this boy.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Could you, in one sentence, answer me this question: Are you saying this young boy was killed by friendly fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 306th and the Frankopan Brigade at the time cooperated. This young boy did not belong to either the 306th or the Frankopan Brigade. He was in this armed group, and incidents between them happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Frankopan Brigade was an HVO brigade; am I right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This young boy was in -- was not in the 306th Brigade but was in Ramo Durmis' unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And Ramo Durmis was part of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. We repeated this on several occasions yesterday. He was not part of any unit of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But he had been part of it at some stage and left?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Much earlier, before this period, he was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade; and with a group of fighters, disagreeing with the policies of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, he left the 7th Muslim Brigade and established his own group, which represented itself variously using different names and falsely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, now I understand. Thank you so much. Sorry, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is still something I cannot understand. You've just mentioned minor incidents between units of the Bosnian Army and units of the HVO, but that doesn't match with what you said; i.e., that Croats had segmented or cut off the various parts of the Bila Valley and that there was -- that was impossible to communicate. This was not a minor incident, so could you please explain what you said when you said that those Croat forces were preventing you from communicating and had cut off the various parts of the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you allow me, perhaps I can help. At this point, I was going to show the witness a document that will clarify this, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I'll be very happy.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 87. For the record, before the document comes up on the screens, this is a document from the Command of the 3rd Corps of 13 April 1993, entitled "Protest."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, could you please --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would ask the document be zoomed in on the one-before-last paragraph of the document in Bosnian and the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please take a look at this part of the document, and I will read a small portion of it. It says: "During the day on April 13th, 1993, HVO units set up new roadblocks and reinforced the existing ones: The Han Bila-Zenica road at Ovnak; the Rudnik-Novi Bila road; the village Pokrajcici, it's not quite clear; Rudnik; the village of Guca Gora on Kosovo; and in front of Guca Gora, several roadblocks on the Guca Gora-Travnik road. During the night between the 13th and 14th of April, 1993, HVO units used small arms fire for provocation purposes." I would like you to explain the following: This is a document dated the 13th of April, 1993. Does this document reflect the situation in the Bila Valley as it was in mid-April 1993, as far as the check-points are concerned?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. Yesterday, I spoke -- I mentioned on several occasions that HVO forces agreed one thing and acted differently. We, within the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, were clear that we could not open a new front in addition to the fighting with the Chetniks, and we tried to avoid conflict in any way possible and reach solutions through agreements. And, unfortunately, although on the one side we reached agreements, on the other hand, in practice, it was quite different, especially after April 8th, when, in Travnik, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was convening a meeting, whose goal was to proclaim the municipalities of Busovaca, Zenica, Vitez, on the 10th of April 1993, which was the date of the anniversary of the independent State of Croatia, to proclaim them independent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. Could we please discuss the following thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit D -- excuse me, document D924.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document dealing with an order from the HVO Brigade Frankopan in Guca Gora of the 24th of April, 1993. Of course, I do not expect you to identify this document. It is a short document, and I would please ask you to read this document. The date is the 24th of May, 1993. Could you please read it and comment on it, but briefly.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is precisely what we are discussing now. The check-points in the Bila Valley that were there, but they were in play of some broader interest, and the dominant elevations at this time were totally under full control of HVO forces, and that is very clear from this order.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that the document that I showed you, as the document which was an order from General Hadzihasanovic, bore the date in early April 1993; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The date on this document was the 3rd of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'm referring here to the order that the witness discussed in relation to the question that was posed by Your Honour, a document where the HVO was mentioned and where it was stated that a conflict with the HVO should be avoided. The date was the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the situation was changing?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe we can, to help the witness answering also this question, we can pull up the document itself, and the witness can have a look at it. There was a lot of information going in, and I think we should all see the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is totally all right; although, I was trying to save time. But before I go back to this document, Your Honour, could we please -- could we please have a number issued for this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document 924 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit 1202.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see now again document D230.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In fact, it does look like D230 was not admitted into evidence yesterday, so just as well it's coming up again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm advised it's been admitted through the Bar Table motion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you see the date? You remember what I asked you a bit earlier when my colleague from the Prosecution made his objection. Do you recall that I asked you about the date of this document? Could you please look at the date, and would you agree that it says there that it's the 3rd of April, 1993? Can you see the date?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I'm not sure whether it's the 3rd or the 5th of April, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please take a look up in the document, where it says "Zenica"?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see there it states the 3rd of April.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you this in relation to the date. This is to clarify the question that Your Honour asked a bit earlier. At this time, in early April 1993, was the corps and the units, you who were on the ground, were you still trying at this time to avoid conflict with the Croats; is that what you were trying to say?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. The way the question was drafted, phrased, it was a leading question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I reply, Your Honour? It would be a leading question if the witness had not already answered this question in detail, the question that Judge Lattanzi posed. A few moments ago, the witness explained in detail that at this time, the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina tried to avoid conflict, and I'm just trying to put -- to draw a tie, put a connection between this document and the questions that Your Honours had yesterday about this. This is the purpose of it; and, therefore, I think this question was not leading, because the witness had already given a reply to it in the same manner that I have interpreted it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would agree with that, Mr. Neuner. Would you not? I thought Madam Vidovic was just taking us back to what the witness already told us a little earlier. So, in that event, I'll allow the question. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, did you understand what I asked you? I asked you whether the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in early April 1993, tried to avoid the conflict. What was the position of the Bosnia and Herzegovina Army on the issue of a conflict with Croats?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At no cost, at no cost were we to open a conflict with the HVO, because we were not strong enough to hold on the lines against the Chetnik-Serbian-Montenegrin aggressor, and the lines of communication and supply routes would have been closed at the same time. In the Bila Valley, locally, this was especially important, because we had no way out and no communication with anyone, except through the territory held by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, it was my understanding that this document has already been assigned a number. Is that correct? I think it was from the Bar Table motion. Thank you. This document may now be removed, and I would like the witness to be shown Exhibit 86.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would you please focus your attention on the part of the document of the 306th Brigade of 11 April 1993, referring to "Own Forces." Would you please take a look, first of all, at the part which says, "In accordance with the previous order ..." "In accordance with the previous order," would you read that, please? There, logistics and logistic support is discussed. And, Witness, I will just quote the last sentence there from this portion. It says there: "Logistics support of the unit is bad, which makes it practically impossible for us to carry out our regular duties." Then mention is made of lack of fuel, lubricants, spare parts, weapons, ammunition, clothing and so on. What I would like to ask you is this: Does this document reflect the actual situation as it was in mid-April 1993 with the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Completely, and this is what we've been discussing throughout.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now look further down in the document, where it mentions the OG West Command. You will see the part which says: "Communications with the OG West Command has been practically nonexistent in approximately the past ten days." What I would like you to do is comment on the situation -- the communications situation in the course of April and May 1993.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The siege [as interpreted] of OG West was in Bugojno. Conflicts with the HVO forces had already started in Bugojno; and, at the time, we didn't have any connection with the OG that we belonged to. This is why our documents and the corps documents from that period of time were addressed both to the corps and to the operations group or the corps. Even though we were part of the operations group, the corps sent the documents directly to the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt my learned colleague. There's just a correction on the transcript. Page 13, line 8, says "the siege of OG West," and I believe the witness has said "the seat of OG West."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Neuner. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thanks to my colleague, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, does this document show the actual state of affairs of communication in the field in the 306th or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, have you heard you've been asked to speak up a little bit?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to talk about June 1993. Please, which military forces were carrying out attacks in the River Bila Valley in June 1993, if any?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of the conflict in the Bila Valley actually happened on the 28th of May, 1993, when -- at the time when the representatives of the Croatian and Bosnian people were negotiating in Guca Gora, very close to the seat of the Frankopan Brigade. During these negotiations, there was an alert given to the Frankopan Brigade units. Their commander, Mr. Ilija Nakic, left the negotiations, and the other negotiators of Croat ethnicity tried to help the Bosniak negotiators, including myself, to pull out safely from Guca Gora. And from that point on, in some 20 places of the Bila Valley, it was absolutely not possible to move, nor was it possible for the locations or localities to communicate amongst themselves, nor was any action possible. The brigade commander, the chief of staff, and his two assistants were blocked, practically captured in the village of Krpeljici in the immediate vicinity of the village of Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you for that very long answer, but can you please answer the question that was put. What forces were operating in the Bila Valley in June 1993? Just tell us the names of the forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO Frankopan Brigade, which at the time was reinforced with the forced Zenica HVO Brigade, and the Jure Francetic Brigade of the HVO, because all those brigades at the time were in the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Were they the only forces in the Bila Valley at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These were the HVO forces, also the 306th Mountain Brigade was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 306th Mountain Brigade, which at that time, because of a general blockade, absolutely was not functioning, except --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Can you please listen to the question, because we haven't got much time. Don't explain what they were doing and what they were not doing. The question is: What forces were involved in the Bila Valley in June 1993? Just give the names of the forces. Don't explain anything. If there's an explanation required, you'll be asked to explain. You said 306th Mountain Brigade, the Frankopan Brigade, with the Jure Franc etic Brigade, and anybody else, any other force?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 1st Zenica HVO Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. There were no other units, but there were members of other --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if I may just clarify, perhaps there was a misunderstanding, so the question is not getting the proper answer. I asked which forces, not which forces were acting. I don't know how it was translated, but "which forces were carrying out attacks in the Bila River Valley in 1993, if any." This question is on page 14, lines 4 and 5. This is why the witness is explaining the actions of the HVO Brigade. Perhaps this is where the misunderstanding lies. I don't know if I've helped. So my question was: Who was carrying out attacks in early June 1993. Your question was who was active, if I'm correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic, but still he should have just been able to mention the names of the forces that were attacking, without giving a long story. That's all I'm asking for.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for your suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, if you can concentrate as much as you can to give simple, direct answers, please.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now look at Exhibit D221, please -- I'm sorry. It's document 221, D221. Can the English text be enlarged. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you can see that this is a telegram. It says the 306th Brigade, Gabela, 910. The date is the 5th of June, 1993. I'm going to quote to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution might be in error; but on the list communicated to us, D221 is not on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, D21 is not there, but D221 is there. Perhaps it was recorded in the transcript erroneously. The number is not clear in the transcript. I'm talking about this document, Your Honours, and this is document D221, at least as far as I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. Your learned friend is throwing his shoulders almost in despair. Mr. Neuner, do you have this document 221 on the list that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The document is not on the list which I have printed out, but I could be flexible if this is helping my colleague. It's not on the list which I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: How are you being flexible?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I could be flexible, please just go on; and if it's possible --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go on, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, thank you, thank you. Is it possible, Your Honours? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, this is a small document. I hope that you've read it. Can you please comment? I wanted to quote a part of the document. It talks about Busovaca, and it says that, "We have 18 dead, six seriously wounded ..." So what I would like to ask you is: Does this reflect the actual situation in the village of Velika Bukovica on the 5th of June, 1993, and could you please also explain to Their Honours what was the ethnicity of the population of Velika Bukovica?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The document reflects the actual state of affairs in Velika Bukovica, where about 100 Bosniak citizens received an ultimatum three days before that to hand over their weapons; and after they failed to do that, they were attacked and they asked for help from the superior command in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who attacked them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Forces of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us where you were in early June --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] excuse me, Your Honours. Can this document be given an exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1203.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, can you please tell us where you were in early June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 28th of May until the 12th of June, with the commander of the brigade and the chief of staff and the assistant for finance, I was cut off or blocked off in the village of Krpeljici, which is between Velika Bukovica and Guca Gora.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you or did you not have contacts with the part of the Command of the 306th Brigade at Rudnik?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only until the end of May. As of June 1st, we did not have contacts with any of our units. We had no control with any of our units or with any other inhabited place.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And what was the situation vis a vis the Corps Command? Were there any contacts with them?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The contacts with the Corps Command were established only by the three duty officers from the main command post of the 306th Mountain Brigade at Rudnik. Up until the time that the Command, on the 6th [as interpreted] of June at 2000 hours in the evening, was shelled; and then after that, even those communications were questionable for a certain period of time. I'm not sure exactly for how long.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, can you stop for a second for me to correct the transcript. It says here that you said that: "On the 6th of June until 2.00 p.m., it was possible to communicate." But I understood you to say that this was possible until the 2nd of June. Was that what you actually said?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you heard me correctly. I did say the 2nd of June, because on the 2nd of June attacks began on these villages, and that was when all the communication was cut off.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you now about the situation in the corps. Did you have contacts with the corps, you, from the place where you were blocked off?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not with the corps or with anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And this part of the brigade that you said was blocked off, where you were also, did you, after the 2nd of June, have contacts with the rest of the brigade at Rudnik?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. Can the witness now look at Exhibit 999, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you can see that this is a document of the 5th of June, 1993, an order sent to the Command of the 306th Brigade and Command of the Bosnian Krajina Operations Group. It's a short document. Can you please read it, and then I will ask you to comment. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document could not have been sent to the brigade commander at the time. The commander was blocked off, and the document actually speaks about the villages of Velika Bukovica, Ricice, and Bandol being attacked. Bandol, at that point in time, was already burned down by the HVO forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just let me ask you, Mr. Husic, what is the basis of your assertion that the commander could not have received this document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 28th, I was continually with the commander, with the chief of staff, and with another colleague, a deputy -- an assistant whose name I mentioned earlier; and we didn't have contacts with anyone until the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can put this document away. I would like the witness now to look at Exhibit 258, please. For the transcript, this is a report and proposals of the Bosanska Krajina Operations Group of the 5th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would ask you, Witness, to focus on the bottom third of the document. This is the English version, the part that begins in the second page of the English version, and, Witness, if you can find the part that begins: "It was ordered for Esed Sipic to organize the units." It's somewhere in the middle of the page. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read that part?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you comment? What is said here is that the communication with Sipic has been cut off, and "we don't have the information if he is already on his way and how far he has come." Can you please comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document could not have been delivered to Sipic because there was no way of establishing the contacts between Sipic and Travnik at that particular time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Can we put this document away now. I would like the witness to look at Exhibit 1000 now, please. For the transcript, this is a response from the 3rd Corps Command, sent to the 306th Brigade, dated the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to read the document and to briefly comment on it. Have you seen this document? Did the brigade actually receive it at that time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is still the time period where Mr. Sipic, as the commander, and I was with him, was unable to receive the document. It could have possibly reached the main command post at Rudnik, but I am not aware of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Can this document be put away, please, and can the witness be shown Exhibit 1001. For the transcript, this is a telegram of the 306th Brigade of the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would also like to ask you to comment as to whether this telegram could have been sent from the place where the commander, the chief of staff, and you were.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please comment on this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been sent only from the main command post at Rudnik, which was also totally isolated, and we did not have any communication with them or the possibility of communication at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. Your Honours, if at this time this document can be put away, and can the witness please look at Exhibit 998.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, before the document appears on the screen, I would like to ask you this: Did you know the signature of the commander of the brigade, Esed Sipic?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown the last page of this document, the last page both in the English and the Bosnian version. The English version, too, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you this: Is what you see here, and you told us that know the signature of Mr. Sipic, is this the signature of the brigade commander, Mr. Esed Sipic?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. We could also see his signature on the previous couple of documents, so it can be compared.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see. Could we now please go back to the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the heading of this document. Is this a complete heading of the document? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is not a heading, because there should be the name of the brigade there, the 306th Brigade, if that's where the document is coming from.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see. Did the documents that the brigade sent go out incomplete, as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you draw some conclusions based on the fact that there is a portion of the heading missing and also that you don't recognise the signature of Mr. Sipic?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is a document from the 306th Brigade, it's possible that it's a draft but not the final document that was accepted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I would now like to ask you one more time, and you talked about the 7th Muslim Brigade yesterday and its presence in the Bila Valley. At the given time that we can see in this document, in mid-May 1993, were there organised parts or units of the 7th Muslim Brigade active in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me -- do you agree with me that, during the proofing, I showed you this document and that you've read it in detail?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see here that some different variants or scenarios are mentioned here in the event of an attack by the Chetnik forces, and then a scenario or a variant of an attack by HVO units?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the second page of the document, please. Yes. This is what the document looks like, Your Honour. This is the second page. It's blank, as it appears here. Could we now see the third page, which will be the third page in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Here, mention is made of a coordinated attack of Chetniks and HVO forces, that variant. Now, let me ask you this: What happened around the 6th of June, 1993, was this in concord with any of the variants that are mentioned here in this document? Does this actually correspond to that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not, because the document mentions here the variants or the scenarios that were theoretically discussed in the brigade from the time when we were aware that there were contacts going on between the Chetniks and the HVO. This was in mid-April 1993. But something quite different happened, and nothing from this document was actually implemented.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you. I don't have any more questions related to this document. Your Honour, this is the time when we are supposed to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. We'll then take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Can the witness be shown Exhibit 234 now. Exhibit 234. And while we're waiting for it to appear on our screens, let me state for the record that this is a report of the head of the Observers Mission, Ambassador Thibault, of the 19th of June, 1993. Please turn to page 4 of the English version and page 4 of the Bosnian version; therefore, page 4 in both versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in the open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Video VD45, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't ask you before asking that the video be played that you stop the video clip whenever you recognise someone.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we rewind the tape a bit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is me.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: We saw this piece of footage. Can you tell us when it was made?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was made on the 11th of June, in the morning hours, at Guca Gora. It was broadcast by the Bosnian TV on the 11th of June at -- in the evening hours at around 1930.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. When was the inside part of the Guca Gora monastery destroyed? I'm talking about the inside.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The footage shows that, at the time when this was filmed, the monastery had not been damaged inside, or rather, its interior had not been damaged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the question that I put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... was made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During this trial, we heard that, at some stage, the inside part of the monastery was destroyed. I was just wondering whether you were in a position to tell me when, if you know. Maybe you don't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, let us clarify something. You heard the question put by Her Honour. It was said that the monastery had been destroyed inside. To your knowledge, in the course of 1993 and onwards, was the monastery -- monastery's interior destroyed; and if so, to what extent?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I believe that Her Honour did not understand the footage, because the anchorperson, before playing the footage, speaks about the fact that the HVO had made it public that the members of the Muslim Forces had destroyed the monastery; whereas, we were filming this in order to deny that piece of information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues] ... because I believe there has been a misunderstanding, and maybe this is my mistake. I am not talking about this video. I could see that, in this video, the monastery doesn't seem destroyed, either inside or outside. What I said is that, during the course of this trial, we were told that the Guca Gora monastery had been destroyed inside the building. If you know, well, you said you didn't know. It's fine. That's all I wanted to know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may be allowed to put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, was this monastery ever destroyed on the inside?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. There was slight damage to it, which implied -- or rather, there was just traces of some greasy paint having been dobbed around and that the organ was damaged and some of the archives of the monastery. But even to this day, one can see that during the war, the interior of the monastery was not destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, was the interior of the monastery ever destroyed during the war?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this video be assigned an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The video is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Registrar's records indicate that this has already been given an exhibit number, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't believe that that is the case. We have only recently received this video footage. Perhaps you're referring to another piece of footage provided to us by the OTP. I don't believe that this is the case in relation to this particular footage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. We apologise. We just made a slight mistake.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document will become Exhibit number 1204.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then the video clip is Exhibit 1204. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us go back to the damage that you referred to? When was it made? You spoke of the paint, of the organ having been damaged, and the archives. When did this take place?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the relevant period; although, I can't tell you precisely when. You know that yesterday we discussed a period of time when occasionally armed groups arrived in Guca Gora and were responsible for the incidents we discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: When it came to these incidents, excesses, or crimes, and I'm speaking of the June of 1993 and onwards, were you able to cooperate with the HVO forces and their commands in obtaining information?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely not. It was not possible to have any cooperation with them, since they refused any contacts.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me now turn to the events in the village of Maline on the 8th of June, 1993. In the month of June of 1993, did you come to learn of some events involving the Croat population of the village of Maline on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We first received word of something having happened there on the 13th of June. At that time, a part of the Command of the 306th met, and the assistant commander for security informed us that there were indications of --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. But the last question, the way it was put, was again a leading one. The witness was directly asked whether some events involving the Croat population in Maline on a particular day he could testify about, and so far this witness has not talked about this event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, Mr. Neuner, it seems to me as if that kind of question is directing the attention of the witness to a particular spot, on a particular date, with respect to a particular population, to tell us what he knows about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is correct, Your Honours. But the way it was phrased, it is particularly put in a particular village, against a particular ethnicity, on a particular day; and an alternative would have been, "What has happened at the beginning of June of 1993," or something like that. But the way this was put, it's directly focusing the witness's attention to talk about one particular incident only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You know, for me, this is an issue that is alleged specifically in the indictment, and I can't see why it cannot be specifically pointed out to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not saying it can't specifically be pointed out. I'm just saying the witness, if he has knowledge about it, would come to it in his testimony, anyway. Just the way this is put now is going to the very heart of the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, that is the alleged thing. It's as good as saying, sir, the accused here is charged with this kind of crime on this particular day, at this particular place, against this particular group. What do you know about it?" It is the same thing as saying that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just wanted to put my observation on the record. I can be overruled by this and I understood that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have another difficulty with this. The witness doesn't answer the questions. Madam Vidovic asked him if on the 8th of June, in Maline, some particular events took place involving the Croat population; and then he says, "Yes." Then he starts talking about another event. So may I invite the witness to answer specifically to the questions put to him by Madam Vidovic. Please avoid telling something about entirely different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. To go back to the objection, the objection is overruled. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I hope you understood this. Could you please answer the question that I posed, whether you learned about some events and what was happening to the part of the village where the Croatian ethnicity lived? This was on the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and that's what I answered the first time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what it is that you learned?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned, on the 12th of June, when, for the first time, a part of the Command of the 306th Mountain Brigade met, the assistant commander for security, Mr. Delalic, stated that, in addition to numerous disinformation that could be heard during the conflict, there were indications that, in the area of Maline and Bikosi, a number of Croatians, people of Croatian ethnicity, were killed. The brigade commander, Mr. Sipic, ordered an investigation into this.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown document D810. For the record, this is a document from the 306th Brigade. Under the text, the date of the 10th of June, 1993 appears.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you read this text, and let's see if you know anything about --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before the witness reads this document, can I put an observation on the record. This was put forward by the Bar Table motion by the Defence; and at the time in the Prosecution's response, we suggested that a fuller translation is provided of that document. As I think it was explicitly stated in the Prosecution's response, this little snippet, it's the second line of the document, "through the network," is, so to speak, in the translation visible, but not in the original. So we, at the time, objected on the basis of this -- to this document, and suggested that a more legible copy would be produced or may be produced by the Defence. And as I can see here, it is still the same copy, so the B/C/S is an incomplete copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, are you able to remember what the decision of the Chamber said on that point?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm not exactly in a position to say now whether the decision contained any particular finding. I just note that this is still a "D," meaning a pre-trial number, so the document was not admitted at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We have seen another "D" document a little earlier, which we were told has already been admitted through the Bar Table motion. So it is quite possible that these documents have not sort of been assigned, what do you call that, exhibit numbers. For me, or for the Trial Chamber, to be able to respond to what you are saying, I would like to know what the decision of the Trial Chamber was on that point. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you want to say something?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to say this: This document was admitted on the basis of a decision by the Trial Chamber of 5 March 2008, but it has not been assigned a number yet. As for what the Prosecutor was saying, that the document is incomplete, I could not agree with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, according to the decision, it looks like it was admitted. And, Mr. Neuner, what is your complaint about this document? What is not legible?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We argued at the time that this, "through the network," which is the upper part of the English translation next to the "231" and circled, that this portion of the document is not reflected in the B/C/S original. There are actually a couple of objections which we had at the time against this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There is something, but nothing which led us to conclude, on the Prosecution side, that this means "through the network." These are illegible items which are displayed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, I see, on the B/C/S, there is something that is not very legible; and then somewhere there is "231" on the same line. It looks like that's your learned friend's basis of objection, that that part is not legible. Do you have anything to say?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, there's nothing I can say. I do not possess a better version at this point in time, and I apologise to the Prosecutor. I will try and see if we can find a better copy. At this moment, I do not have it; but in any case, I will not ask the witness anything about this part of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And maybe, then, the logical solution would then be to strike out "through the network" in the English version for the time being, until --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This document has been admitted through a decision of the Trial Chamber of the 5th of March, 2008. The Trial Chamber would like to add that the words "through the network" on the English version be struck out, for the reason that the B/C/S version thereof is illegible and it is not possible to determine whether those are the words mentioned in the B/C/S. Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I hope you were able to read this document while we were having this discussion. Do you have any idea what these letters "DR" at the bottom of the document mean?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read the document. These are the initials of the assistant commander for security in the 3rd Corps, Dugalic, Ramiz.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You can see the date here, 10 June 1993. That's below the text. Tell us, please, how would you comment on this document? Does this correspond to what you knew about the events at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned about this event a bit later, because I was cut off in the Krpeljici village, and this was the time when we were just beginning to be able to move around. But this does correspond to what was happening at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me, was the Brigade Command informed of the outcome of the investigation? My understanding was that Commander Sipic had ordered an investigation. As the command, did you get any feedback, and what was it?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We did get information about this at the first meeting of the Command following the event, this was on the 15th of June, 1993, when the assistant commander for security, Mr. Delalic, informed the commander that the result of the investigation showed the following: That a group of armed and masked individuals, whose identity the military police of the 306th Brigade was unable to determine, intercepted the military police of the 306th Mountain Brigade while they were escorting this column of Croatian people towards the village of Mehurici; and under threat of arms, even pointing or putting the muzzle of the weapon into the mouth of one policeman, took away a number of Croats from them. And, at this time, because of all the disinformation that we mentioned earlier, and mention was made of a huge number of people, tens of people killed in different areas, we could not find out anything more in any detail. I think that he learned at the time what the number of people concerned was. I can't quite tell you now, but I think about 20.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was it established, according to what you know, who the perpetrators were or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We really wanted to establish this, both the police and the Security Service, but also other services of the brigade. Because this was addressed to us, this was at our expense because it had happened in our area of responsibility. All of these services really wanted to establish the truth. I know this because we sent policemen, who had been intercepted. We sent them to try and identify, among these -- from among these armed groups, to identify the people by observing those areas where they moved -- through which they're moved. However, we were never able to find out the exact information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just want to ask this question before this part of the evidence disappears. You said, sir, at line 20 of page 38: "Yes. We did get information about this at the first meeting of the Command following the event." Now, my question to you is: Who did you get this information from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the first meeting of a part of the Command, the assistant commander for security, Asim Delalic, informed on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, do I understand you to say that the military police of the 306th Brigade, from whom these people were taken, made no report on the day the event took place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I don't know when they drafted their report; but the brigade commander and I, the chief of staff and the assistant for finance, we met and we discussed this separately, separate from the other parts of the unit, so that we didn't know of this earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you know whether the military police of the 306th Brigade, from whom these people were taken, ever made a report at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When was that report made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 15th of June, the assistant commander for security informed, in other words, the commander, the brigade commander, ordered him to sent a report to the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Listen to the question. Did the military police of the 306th Brigade make a report about this incident to your Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could not have any insight into what the military police was doing. The assistant commander for security reported on their activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the security police. If you know about the military police making a report, tell us that you know, because you said you do know a little earlier. If you don't know, say you don't know. Please, we want short answers here. My question is such that, you can say "yes" or "no," you don't know whether the military police made a report at all about this incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me just ask you a bit more, so that we clarify this. Did you know the way the brigade functioned?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you know who was the superior to the military police, so whom did the military police report to?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the assistant commander for security.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm just seeing so far the two questions, they are not dangerous, as such, but they are again phrased in a leading way. Maybe my colleague can just ask, "Who was the superior," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I really should be a magician to phrase my questions this way. I have to specify which part of the brigade I'm talking about. I'm talking about the military police, and I have to ask who their superior was. I don't see any other way that I could phrase this question, and I really would appreciate -- I do understand that the Prosecutor is doing his job, but also we have a limited time for this -- for this questioning. We are just wasting time with these objections. I really feel that the last two objections are absolutely ungrounded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We're going to deal with this last one objection, not the two. The question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, I just don't remember what you responded. I asked you to whom the military police submits a report.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I answered the assistant commander for security; and in this case, that was Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What you testified -- actually, who did you find out from about these events?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found this information out also from the assistant commander for security, Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to ask you the following: What were the results of the investigation, in terms of the perpetrators? Was it known to whom, or to which unit, they belonged, more or less?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I explained this earlier. They were -- they belonged to the foreign forces, but we don't know which unit it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a question. The military police belonging to your unit, was this military police obligated to report to their higher body, but by according to the function?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In this case, this was actually the assistant commander for security who submitted the report to his superior; and his superior, actually with this document that we are looking at on the screen, was asking him precisely to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, do you know if at a later stage there was an investigation conducted into these events?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And why don't you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is not in my purview. We had other duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to move to a different topic. I'm going to ask you about some events from 1995. When you provided your particulars for the transcript, you said that you worked in the morale sector of the 3rd Corps Command. Do you remember from when you performed these duties?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I came to this post in late February or early March of 1994, to this section for morale, propaganda, and religious affairs. At the time, I was deputy to the assistant commander. Later, I became assistant commander in the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please briefly describe exactly what your area of work was?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our work, in the morale section, is quite broad. First of all, it was our duty to act politically and to explain the platform and the objectives of our fight. Each soldier had to have an explanation that the objective of our struggle was a united, unified, and indivisible Bosnia-Herzegovina. We also needed to inform fighters about all the events, gather information that had to do with combat readiness in units. And if anything needed to be done in that respect, and to affirm our struggle in such a way, that we would explain that the International Community would be on the side of that army that would adhere to all international laws and the Geneva Conventions, and which had the backing and support of the people, which does not sew and disseminate fear, or does not destroy, burn, or in any other way destroy and violate these general principles that were put before us. We acted on duties to inform, to combat hostile propaganda, the welfare of the families, the care of fighters after wounding, and we carried out many other duties, too.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in that sense, were you receiving instructions or orders from the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, regularly, always, both instructions and orders. We had training sessions and seminars pursuant to plans that they drafted.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. A little bit earlier, speaking about the range of your duties, you said that you also dealt with the question of fighters who were killed, but I actually want to ask you something else. What was the position of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina leadership in terms of enemy soldiers? So I'm not talking about the soldiers of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'd like you to focus on the position of the Supreme Command Staff and the command of your corps, in terms of enemy soldiers.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was clear right from the start that fighting for a united, indivisible Bosnia-Herzegovina and its three peoples implied winning over the people. By sowing fear and hatred and killings, this could not be achieved. So, in order to stimulate the soldiers to kill as few enemy soldiers as possible, we, at the time -- actually, we gave 25 monthly soldiers' salaries for each captured enemy soldier in order to motivate the fighters, whenever they had the opportunity, instead of killing, to capture enemy fighters, so that in that way we would be different from those forces who were destroying and blowing apart Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You gave them 25 what? The transcript is not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We gave them the amount in marks, which was the currency in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time, amounting to the sum of 25 soldiers' monthly salaries.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: For what?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For each captured enemy soldier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Twenty-five soldiers' monthly salaries. You gave that to who, to the whole unit, or to share, or to one person, one soldier who captured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Each individual who captured an enemy soldier, pursuant to an order of the commander --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. They would receive --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They received the salary of twenty-five soldiers. A very rich army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The standard in Bosnia and Herzegovina at the time was very low. Our salaries were just 4 marks. But for each captured soldier, the person who captured the soldier, I'm talking about captured enemy soldiers, that person who captured the enemy soldier would receive 100 marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. We understand you better now. Thank you. Now we would like you to look at Exhibit [as interpreted] D1002, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, while we're waiting for the document to appear, this is a document of the 3rd Corps Command, dated the 10th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Madam Vidovic. I'm sorry to do this. The transcript says "Exhibit D1002." Is it a document or an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "D", Your Honour. This not an exhibit. I don't know if I said "Exhibit."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The transcript says so.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I would like you to look at this document and to tell us if you recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document from the commander's office, from the General Staff. We passed it down to our subordinate units from the 3rd Corps, and this document was sent out via my section.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to ask you --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the bottom of the document, please. Can we scroll down to see the entire document, both in English -- in the English, actually, it's page 2. It's the next page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to ask you is this: Can you briefly explain the principle of passing down documents? What happens to a document? How does a document reach you, and then what happens after that with it? How is it disseminated further, if it is disseminated?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about a document of the superior command, we would receive this document with a packet communication. We would look at it; and if it was a document for subordinate units, we would then place or mark it as something that should be delivered to all units or dispatched to all units. Then we would send it to the office, where all the documents were typed and disseminated further. The documents that were being drafted for the superior command, after they would be processed and completed, we would also send to the office; and, sometimes, it was enough just to place an arrow facing down to indicate that it was going to subordinate, lower-ranking unit, or an arrow facing up, indicating that it was going to the superior command, so that you did not have to write down each time on the document something that was known or implied.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Who authored this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document came from the Supreme Command Staff, so I cannot know who authored it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It says, "Halid Husic." I just wanted to be sure --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am the one who dispatched it further. I am not the person who drafted the document. I just dispatched or forwarded the document. I don't know who wrote it in the Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: This "Halid" here refers to you. Actually, it's "Halid Husic," and it should have been "Halim Husic."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to go back to the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what this document is seeking or requesting?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to the previous page on the English -- in the English version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With this document, the State Commission for the Exchange of Prisoners, through the General Staff, was asking all the units of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina to -- or asking that all the captured enemy soldiers are not killed, and that as soon as the information or the particulars of the captured soldiers should be sent to them as soon as, because this service for the exchange of prisoners of war needed to have this information. This was something that we worked on intensively.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We would like to ask you to read this first dashed paragraph. I'm actually going to quote. It says that The commands of all corps of the RBiH Army and the commands of all their subordinated units be advised to capture members of the enemy formations in all situations when the lives and health of the members of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina are not jeopardised. Then the members of these formations are listed.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this fit within the general objectives of our fight, and this is something that we discussed and intensely worked on.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document will become Exhibit number 1205.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And, Madam Vidovic, while I'm on the floor, minus questions by the Chamber and other people, the four hours of Defence have about five to seven minutes remaining.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't have too many questions left, but I don't believe I will be able to cover all of them in five to seven minutes. But I will do my best to finish as soon as possible. I will definitely keep that in mind. Well, I don't remember now if we did get an exhibit number for this document. Okay. Very well. Maybe we can show the witness now the Exhibit 1047. For the transcript, this is a document of the morale sector of the 3rd Corps, dated the 25th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: First of all, Witness, do you see this document, and do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see this is a document that I forwarded, and this is my signature on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we please zoom in on the bottom part of the document. In the English version, I think that this is on the following page. Your Honours, I would like the witness now to look at the initials here. In the electronic version, you cannot really see them that easily, so I would like the witness very quickly to be shown the hard copy of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, can you look at the initials on the document? I'm going to ask you something about that a little later. Can you see if this document is signed or not?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not signed, and the initials are "MM." It's Mustafa Music, who was the clerk in the Supreme Command Staff, Morale Department.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 3 in the English, please. Your Honours, I have just asked for this to be shown. It's page 3 of the English version. Can you please scroll up? All right. Very well. This is good.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Mr. Mustafa Music. Witness, I don't know if this was recorded in the transcript. Yes, it was. You said that this document is not signed. Do you know why that is so?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not the customary method of work of the Morale Department, that the commander should be signing this document. These documents are usually signed by the assistant commander. In this particular case, that is not the case. We have the commander in the signature, but it doesn't actually have a signature, and it's a little bit unusual in that sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
