utterances.text: Let me ask you this, Mr. Husic: In case this was an encoded document, would you be able to see who actually signed the document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was this document encoded?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, actually, I wouldn't say that it was encoded. I don't see that it was encoded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we scroll down the document so that the Trial Chamber can look at this. Can we go back to the first page of the document, please. You can look at the English version, the top part of the document, where we could see if there are any indications that the document was encoded. Can we also look at the top part of the Bosnian version. Is that the entire document that you can see? Thank you. There are no such markings, so, Your Honour, this document can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Husic, I would like to ask you -- I have some questions, I don't have much time, about the July action in Vozuca in 1995. Did you play any role in this action?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. At this time, I was at the Orahovo IKM, and I was with the -- en route with the forces of the 3rd Corps towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown document D863. You can see that this is a document from 23rd August 1995, signed by Mufti Effendi Halil Mehtic. I would like to ask you is this: What was the relationship between the Effendi Halil Mehtic in 1993 up until the end of the war, if any [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber what a mufti is?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A mufti is a clerical duty, a duty of a cleric that would be equivalent to a bishop in the Catholic Church.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please -- can I just goat back to the transcript. I think my question was omitted. Now I can see it, yes, I think it has been. Your Honour, give me just a moment, please. My question that did not clearly -- that was not clearly written down in the transcript was: Was there any kind of relationship between the mufti, Mehtic, Halil Mehtic, and the corps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, except the relationships that the corps had with any other institution, the civilian authorities, the clerk authorities, with respect to those services that were provided by those institutions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now explain to the Trial Chamber what the title of "Mufti" exactly means?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Islamic community, the mufti is equivalent to a bishop in the Christian or Catholic Church for a certain area.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is "Effendi" a name of a person or is it also a title in the Muslim religion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] it is a title.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is its equivalent in the Catholic Church?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A cleric, a priest, any religious person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it is acceptable, in the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The honourable reverend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it acceptable, in the Muslim religion, to call a person "Mufti Effendi" or "Effendi Mufti," so-and-so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The order of these titles has its own logic, in the same manner that in the civilian life, professors and doctors are addressed with certain titles. The Halil Effendi Mufti Mehtic means "the honourable mufti", and if we add his duty, then we know this is an official cleric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And his duty would be mufti?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I have a question, too. Witness, please, you said that the civilian authorities would provide services to the military institutions. Could you give us some details on this and tell us what services were provided to the military institutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Civilian authorities would provide arms and logistic support to the army. Cultural institutions would help in organizing entertainment and cultural events in the army. Religious institutions and persons would help in organizing the religious life within units. But this document that we see before us has nothing to do with that. This is something completely different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I was not referring to this document. It's just after an answer that you gave us. About what you said, there is another thing I would like to know. I would like to know whether the local civilian institutions also provided premises where units could be billeted, for example.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, let's just go back to the content of this document. Looking at it, it would appear that the mufti is issuing a certificate that a member belonged to the armija and, as such, was killed at the Vozuca battlefield. Could you give a comment on the document?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All army members -- for all army members, the command -- the garrison command would issue certificates, but only in those cases where someone who may have been a foreigner and not a member of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. For those persons, we did not issue certificates. They were issued by some other institutions; and, in this case, it was by the mufti. The fact that he mentioned there that someone was a member of something, that's his problem, because was he a member -- had he been a member of the army, he would not have been issued a certificate by the mufti.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, could we please have a number assigned for this document. This is, again, a document that was entered through the Bar Table, so I just want to make sure that it doesn't receive two numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, I would just briefly like to dwell on the Farz action, and I hope the Prosecutor will not say that this is a leading question. Did you participate in any activities related to the Farz action on the Vozuca battlefield in 19 -- in September 1995?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As part of the 3rd Corps Command, I participated actively in the preparation and carrying out of the Operation Farz.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said "preparations." Could you please describe briefly what you mean?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean preparations and planning for combat activities, which means that in all segments, in my case the segment dealing with combat morale, a plan should be drafted for morale support for this action, which implied the implementation in all units that were participating in this operation, and support in implementing it and controlling it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us, in these preparations for an action, was there -- did anything deal with the conduct of combatants with their handling of war prisoners?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We again, before every action, which was the case every time, we would again carry out morale preparations. We insisted, what we could see earlier through some of the documents, that they should refrain from killing, that they should capture enemy combatants, and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recall, did you personally participate in combat activities within the Farz OPERATION?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the first day of the combat operation, we entered the combat operation zone, and the assistant commander for operations and planning --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I just want to put it on the record, the last two questions were again leading. The witness has already answered, so I didn't stand up at the first one, and this one is the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may respond. I really don't know how to phrase my questions except to ask the witness if he had participated in these combat actions. Perhaps my colleague can assist me. How would I phrase this question on the witness's participation and involvement on this operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just you may wish to ask, "How were you participating in Operation Farz, which you mentioned," and then the witness goes on; or, "In your morale section, what were you doing in order to participate in Operation Farz?"

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness described what he did. What the Prosecutor suggested just now, how I should phrase my question, that would, indeed, be a leading question. All I asked was whether he participated in the Farz operation, and the witness replied. So I really think we're just wasting time on these objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, I guess the Prosecutor's question is, "What were you doing," not, "Were you doing A, B, C, D?" Your question was, "Did you personally participate in combat activities?" That's the basis of his objection. He starts his question with a, "What, what were you doing?" You sort of suggested he was participating in combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. But that's the only fact that I mentioned there in order to elicit a response that really have to do with some other questions that I feel are important. Perhaps I could have gone about this in such a way as to lose some five minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As I indicated the other day, if we do it correctly the first time, then we gain time. If you do it incorrectly, then your learned friend keeps standing up and we lose more time. Shall we take a break at this stage and come back at quarter to 6.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We discussed the Farz action, and I would like to ask you the following: Where were you, if you can recall, on the 10th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was at the command post of the 35th Division, at the place called "Babylon."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how long did you stay in these areas where the combat activities were going on?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only entered the area of the combat activities during the day, and I stayed there for about four to five hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I was referring to days. I wanted to know how many days you stayed in that area?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area, I remained a bit longer, but I was not within the zone of the combat activities. In that zone, I spent only one day.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I want to ask you the following: During these combat activities, within the Farz operation or after it, did you get any information about some war prisoners, prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Among other things, because the morale section, by its function during the combat activities, have nothing to do with the prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What day was it when you were in the zone of activity, this one day you say you were in the zone of activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was on the 10th of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You said, on the 10th of September, you were at the IKM of the 35th Division in Babylon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that is the place, Babylon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that where the activity was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A few kilometres before this place was where the combat activities were being carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: During these combat activities, did you communicate, did you have contact with Fadil Hasanagic, the division commander?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the Corps Command, Mr. Ribo and I were at his command post also before the combat activities began and also on the day when the combat activities actually started. We were together at his command post.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And do you remember the next day and the day after; do you remember where you were then?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because we had a number of wounded and killed soldiers, we, from the section for morale, went to the hospital to visit the wounded soldiers in order to and also to make arrangements for the burial of those who were killed in action.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could the witness now be shown Exhibit 411. This is a document from the Morale Administration, dated 24 September 1995, and entitled: "Report on a visit of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina units which participated in the most recent battles for liberation by the ARBiH General Staff commander, Army General Rasim Delic." I would like to ask you this: Have you ever seen this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll repeat myself. Could we please see the English version showing the content of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see it now, Your Honour? Your Honour, for now, I only read the title of the document, and you can see it in the English version. I would now like to ask for the next page of the document to be shown. That is page 2 in the Bosnian version and page 3 of the English version. Page 2 of the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, would you please look at item 7 of this document. I will quote it, and I think we will gain time that way. So item 7 of this document says the following: "Through the cooperation of the Army of RBiH Corps, coordinated and successfully orchestrated by the ARBiH General Staff, the operation has shown the strength and lethal capacity of the Army of RBiH in general, including its ability to carry out the largest possible operations." What I would like to ask you is this: Is this document correct in this segment?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one from the General Staff, during the operation but also during the planning phase of the action, while we were working at the command post in Zenica, operated or participated in these activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I see. And can you tell me, who commanded, as far as you know, in these operations, in these actions, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commanders of the 3rd Corps, Mr. Mahmuljin; and the commander of the 2nd Corps, Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last word? The interpreter did not hear him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness is requested to repeat the last word. He was not heard.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 2nd Corps was commanded by the commander of the 2nd Corps, Mr. Saed Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, I would now like to ask you something quite different. We've seen a number of documents which showed that documents were forwarded to the El Mudjahedin Detachment. I would like to ask you this: While you were at the head of the morale section, did the El Mudjahedin Detachment forward any report to you relating to morale?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is again a leading question. It suggests to say, "Yes." My learned colleague is asking very precisely whether the El Mujahedin unit did certain things. So far, the witness has not talked about the El Mujahedin Detachment forwarding a report. It's already a very specific question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I've been saying this before as well. I'm just trying to save time, and I will rephrase it. It will get me to my answer faster.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you please describe to me the reporting relationship between the El Mudjahedin Detachment and your morale section, if there was anything like that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the beginning to the end of my stay in the 3rd Corps, we never received a single report from the El Mudjahedin Detachment. We didn't even know who was the person in the unit in charge of morale. They didn't inform us about that, either.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to talk about the measures to -- or incentives for soldiers. How were these incentives suggested? Who made these proposals?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The incentives [as interpreted] were sent from the lower units up to the higher commands. We would make a list and a selection, then to finally decide on the list of those who would actually receive these incentives.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like us to look at Exhibit 111 now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just understand the last answer before we go to this exhibit. The answer says: "The incentives were sent from the lower units up to the higher commands." So the lower units were advising the higher commands?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Proposals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That makes a difference. Proposals of people who were to receive incentives were sent from the lower command to the higher command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The proposal of the units who, from their collective, has excelled and would deserve to receive this incentive. These proposals came up from the lower units, then higher commands would make a selection. They would reduce the number until they reached the final list of those who would actually receive the incentives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please now look at this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, this is a nomination for commendations and incentives from the 3rd Corps Command, dated the 10th of November, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, after we look at the first page, can we please look at page 6 in the Bosnian version, and this is page 7 in the English version. We need to look at the signature line.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is this document signed?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a draft version, and it's not signed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to page 2 of the document, both in the Bosnian and in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this. Do you recognise anything here?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is exactly what I was talking about. This is the draft of the document, so you see added in hand that someone is being transferred from one incentive category to another. Some names are added by hand, which actually indicates what I was talking about, that this is a draft version of the document. The final document had a much smaller number of incentives, because the units would usually exaggerate and the higher commands would reduce this number.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just wish to add that this document was tendered by the Prosecutor, and these additions by hand are something that you do not have in the English version. We just have in one place where it is written "Effendi Mahmut Karalic." This was translated, but these arrows and some other markings are not indicated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct, Witness?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was not sent out like this, because some names were removed, some were changed in terms of the type of incentives, and some other things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In principle, were these large documents or smaller, shorter documents that you would send to the Supreme Command?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be an enormous document in the draft version, but then the final version would be a document of only a few pages of text.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We can put this document away. I would now like you to look at Exhibit 1134, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm sorry, Mr. Registrar. Can you keep the previous document just one second more on the screen, because it suddenly caught my attention that there are a few names of people here who are being proposed for a prize or whatever it is from the Mujahedin, if you look at number 30 and 31 and 32. My question for the witness, therefore, would be: How would that come about? There would have to be some sort of cooperation and reporting from the El Mujahid Detachment to the 3rd Corps for you to be able or for the 3rd Corps to be able to produce a list that would include promotions or appraisals for members of the El Mujahid Detachment. So how was that carried out in practice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this case, the proposals came through the units to which they were resubordinated in a given situation. So the 35th Division sent this particular proposal. They put the proposal to the 35th Division. The 35th Division put the proposal to the corps. Then it was further reduced at the corps, which then sent it to the higher command, in turn, to the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: If I understand this correctly, then, there would have been some sort of communication or contact between the 35th Division and the El Mujahid Detachment, would there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In other situations, also, when it suited them, they would establish contact, but we, as superior commands, would regularly do everything for them that we did for the other units, in the sense that we would send them all kinds of documents, attempting to place them under control, to turn them into soldiers, and other activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just understand. Do I understand you to be saying that there were occasions when the 3rd Corps would jump the 35th Division and communicate directly to the El Mudjahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So then I don't understand your last answer. You're saying: "In other situations, also, when it suited them, they would establish contact, but we, as superior commands, would regularly do everything for them that we did for the other units, in the sense that we would send them all kinds of documents, attempting to place them under control." I would expect those documents would come from the 3rd Corps to the 35th Division and the 35th Division would pass them on." Now, you're saying, no, there was no such direct communication. How, then, do you explain your previous answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] when this unit, and this time when these incentives were being proposed, so when this unit was part of the 35th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not talking about that, the incentives. I'm talking about - let me just hold it before it goes - I'm talking about these occasions when you'd regularly do everything for them that you did for other units, in the sense that you would send them all kinds of documents. That's what I'm talking about. I'm not talking about the incentives. How do you explain that answer, if you say you never communicated directly with them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We did send it to them directly, all materials, but we did not receive return reports back from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: My question is: Which of these two versions must the Chamber accept? I asked you a question a couple of minutes ago, "Did you send them communication directly," and you said, "No." Now you say, yes, you did send them. Now, which one must we accept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lease, there were times when they were not subordinated to the 35th Division and they were directly under the control of the 3rd Corps. That's when we directly communicated with them. And when they were in the 35th Division, then we would communicate with them via the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then I think, you see, you can't conflate those two situations into one answer. You've got to clarify that, when you did communicate directly with them, it was when they were not resubordinated to the 35th Division. You can't want to throw in the 35th Division when it suits you, and then when it doesn't, say, no, they communicated with them directly, without explaining that that would happen at a time when they were not so subordinated to the 35th Division. Proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would like the witness now to look at Exhibit 1134, please. For the transcript, this is a document of the 23rd of December, 1995. It's a document of the General Staff of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention, Witness, to the introductory part of the document, which states - can you please look at the opening paragraph of the document - that the order is pursuant to an order by the 3rd Corps commander of the 23rd of December, 1995. I would like to ask you to tell us everything that you know about this proposal, if you know anything, and to explain the context in which the proposal came about, if you know?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This proposal did not go through the regular procedure, through the morale organ or the personnel organ, as it would in the regular procedure. The date of the document, when the commander of the 3rd Corps is directly proposing something, and his secretary, because her initials are here, did work on this document, all of that indicates that this is a time period when we were undertaking activities to abolish the El Mujahid Detachment in order to get on the good side of its members who were opposed to this position of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Among other things, they -- these incentives were granted, and this was done in an extraordinary procedure in the period immediately prior to the Dayton Accords, when it was necessary to disband this unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us -- you said that you wanted to get on the good side of the unit. Why was this necessary?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time when they found out that the unit was going to be disbanded, they openly said that they would oppose such an order, that they would continue the war. I know when the 3rd Corps commander at one time told a few of them that, in that case, they could just do that only disobeying him and his entire units. The 3rd Corps commander was a very tactful man. He knew that they enjoyed support among the people. War was about to end imminently, and we were faced with the danger of a completely new conflict breaking out between the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina and this unit, which would probably be backed by a considerable number of the citizens from that area. The unit would be backed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to put one more question to you. In the Morale Department of the 3rd Corps during the war, did you ever receive an order -- did you ever find out, rather, that the El Mudjahedin Detachment had committed any criminal act, yes or no? Did you receive such information?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. The witness has already answered. The Prosecution believes that this was, again, a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that it's not a leading question. I asked did he or did he not, the witness or his department, ever receive information about criminal activities. I don't see how else I could put this question to the witness without losing ten or 15 minutes of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The question is allowed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Just one more time. I don't know, Witness, if you heard what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard the question, and I already answered it. No, we never did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have information of any kind about the negative attitude of this unit towards prisoners of war or towards civilians?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We did not have information like that at all. No information indicated or even intimated such events.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, the Defence has no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My name is Matthias Neuner. I'm appearing here on behalf of the Prosecution. I'm going to put a couple of questions to you; and if you don't understand certain questions, please ask me to rephrase them, and I will try to do so. First of all, I wanted to talk about the 306th Mountain Brigade. Do you agree with me that the 306th Mountain Brigade was no manoeuvre unit during the war?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was not a manoeuvre unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This brigade had its own area of responsibility, and the soldiers on duty stayed within the area of responsibility of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question because I don't understand the contents of the meaning of the term "area of responsibility." I'm not a professional soldier, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the area of responsibility or the territory covered by the 306th Brigade was a part of the Bila Valley during the war?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And soldiers of the 306th Brigade used to be on the front lines in this territory covered by the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Occasionally, yes, but not all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If soldiers of the 306th Brigade were on duty, they did not travel outside the Bila Valley for certain combat activities?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on Vlasic or the Bila Valley. The 306th Mountain Brigade was at an elevation of 1.800 metres, and they held their lines there permanently, facing the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the 306th Brigade was a territorially-based unit?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer this question. I don't know what it means, actually, that it was a territorial unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will withdraw the question. The 1st Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade was stationed in Mehurici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the 1st Battalion in June 1993 of the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that Mirzet Ljubenovic was the commander at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And who was the commander of the 4th Battalion of the 306th Mountain Brigade in June of 1994 -- excuse me, 1993? I misspoke.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the commanders of the 4th Battalion replaced one another frequently, so it's hard for me to say who was the commander at that time. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you tell me where the 4th Battalion was based of the 306th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th Battalion was based -- or rather, its command post was on the premises of the elementary school in the Visnjevo village, and the fighters were billeted in private homes when they were not on duty. They were in their own homes, staying with their own families.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And these fighters were coming from the villages of Dub, Suhi Dol, Orahovo, Visnjevo, and Jezerci; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. No, not Jezerci. I apologise. Visnjevo, Dub, Suhi Dol, Orahovo, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to come to your testimony about your position as assistant commander for morale. I understand you became the assistant commander for morale in the 306th Brigade in March 1993, yes?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the establishment of the 306th, I was the assistant commander for morale, and we, as the command, we established the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was asking whether in March 1993 you assumed that post in the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As assistant commander for morale in the 306th Mountain Brigade, I was appointed in ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure of the month.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: ... 1993; and together with other members of the command, I worked on the establishment of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you repeat again the month you were appointed, please, for the interpreter?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: November 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the first half -- or throughout 1993, who was your superior in the Morale Department in OG Bosanska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, we were not -- throughout this period, we were not part of the Bosanska Krajina Operations Group. Secondly, the assistant commander's name in the Bosanska Krajina Operations Group, the assistant commander for morale, I cannot really recall now, because we - and you can see that from the documents as well - we were subordinated to them for a very brief period, or rather, while we were subordinated, we were not -- we were not able to communicate with them because all the contacts had been broken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I now remember that you testified and you were shown a couple of documents from OG West. Did you have a superior in OG West; and if so, what was his name, in 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in the Operations Group West, there was someone who was an assistant -- his assistant; but we never had any physical contact, because the seat of this operations group was very far away and the communication was never possible. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you have a superior in the 3rd Corps section for morale in 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What was the name?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His name was Professor Dr. Faik Uzunovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And within the 306th Brigade Morale Service, how many subordinates did you have?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Brigade Command itself, there were five of us, occasionally six or seven, depending on what time we're talking about. Each battalion had two, and the company had one person for morale. We called them "the morale people."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, throughout your testimony you mentioned that certain persons had contact with the Mujahedin, were there some members in the morale section of the 306th Brigade who had such contacts?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not as far as I know, because their relationship towards me and my relationship with them was rather tense, so that at the time when we were establishing the brigade, even the private contacts that we had in the beginning were now not so good.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You told us yesterday that, initially, the Mujahedin had asked you to work at one of their schools. Could you tell me, who asked you?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not say this yesterday. The Mujahedin were billeted at the elementary school in Mehurici on orders of the civilian authorities of the Travnik Municipality; and via the civilian structures --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I wasn't asking you for the reason why they were based at the Mehurici school. I was just interested in who at the time had asked you or approached you and asked you to work at their school.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Mujahedin, one of them whose name was Abdullah, he was in charge of education. He came to my house and asked that I and my wife work for them or with them in their school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where was Abdullah living at the time?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was in Mehurici, in the school building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you were asked to work in which school?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They organised in every village in private houses. They would lease one room, and they would call it the school. They organised -- in these rooms, they organised training, instruction, and one such room was also in my uncle's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, when were you approached, approximately?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was - I cannot pinpoint it exactly - late in the autumn of 1992; October, perhaps November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, could you elicit from the witness whether the witness responded positively to the request from the Abdullah? Was any arrangement ever made? Did the MD rent a room in the witness's house?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you please try to answer the Judge's question? What response -- sorry. What response did you give the -- did you give Abdullah?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I declined this invitation, or rather, I made it conditional on the premise that we would work based on the literature that was at the time used in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They did not accept this, and this is why I did not accept their offer, their invitation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could you tell me, where was the house of your relative where they rented a room, the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was very close to the house where my parents used to live in the past. This was in Dub village. But at this time, it was abandoned, the house, because my parents at this time lived in Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And Dub is in the Bila Valley, a village a little bit above Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the northwest some five, six, perhaps ten kilometres from Han Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You testified about the presence of the Mujahedin in Mehurici school. Could you tell me, when did the Mujahedin first move into Mehurici school?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, because, at this time, I was not in Bosnia and Herzegovina. They arrived there before me, and I talked about this earlier. And when the incident occurred, when my relative called me and asked me to protect the school's property, this was at the end of May or beginning the June in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you're telling us that the Mujahedin had moved into the school already before May 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not before May. That was not possible. I arrived there at the end of May. They had arrived there a little before me. But this was in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you also, testified at some point in time, the Mujahedin moved out of the school to Poljanice. When, approximately, did the Mujahedin leave the Mehurici school?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but around the time of new year 1992-1993, because for the needs of the brigade, we have the need to billet the battalion, we billeted the battalion there, and they were -- they clashed with them, so they left the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And yesterday, and this is page 61 and 62 of the transcript, you said: "I did not personally go to Poljanice and communicate, but some people that they tolerated better or respected more, we would send such people to their unit." My question I'm having is: Could you tell me who, in the 306th Brigade, made the decision to send somebody to the -- to Poljanice to talk to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one from the brigade made that decision; but, rather, through the civilian authorities and the local clerics, we tried, on several occasions, to draw their attention to some things that were happening in our area of responsibility. The problem was this: The officers of the 306th Brigade were not officers that they accepted as someone to talk to. They were afraid of us, and they considered that we were spying on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you're saying that no member of the 306th Brigade talked to the Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in that way. So no one was sent before the brigade, because there was a number of people who later left our unit, to join them; and, of course, they couldn't go there before -- without having previously communicated with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But people who stayed within the 306th Brigade, were they talking to the Mujahedin in Poljanice?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Officially, no, in this period of time. Whether someone did, and I also had done so before, but when they stopped communicating with me, then I wasn't able to do it anymore. But, officially, from the Command, we could not communicate with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When did official communications by members of the 306th Brigade with the Mujahedin start?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. I do not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness replied. However, at no point, until now, did the witness mention that there were any official communications between the 306th Brigade and the Mujahedin, and there is no foundation for this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, if you look at page 77, line 24, the witness answers: "Officially, no, in this period of time." Now, for me, reading that sentence, it leaves me with the impression that, in another period of time, there was such official contact, so I would then want to know what time was that. And if that impression is wrong, then the witness can say, "No, you misunderstood my answer."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understood it the same way, and I understood from you that there was no official communication with the Mujahedin at all by the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Are you referring to 1993 -- sorry, 1992 and 1993, or you're referring to the entire war?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both 1992 and 1993. But toward the end of 1993, I left the 306th Brigade, and I cannot know about the period after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Is it correct that in 1993, in the Bila Valley, there were a couple of different units, military units?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic. Sorry, sorry, sir. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we can -- if this question can be more specific, because it's very general. What units did he mean, the BH Army, the HVO? What did he mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I was referring to units fighting on the side of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's better.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] between the 306th and other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Next to the 306th, there was also the 312th Brigade, is that correct, in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The 312th Brigade was in Travnik. Several individuals from the Bila Valley were members of that 312th Brigade from Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: There were also -- or not "also." There was also the 314th Brigade which had a battalion in the Bila Valley; correct?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 314th Brigade had locals from Zagradje, Skomorje --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not sure this is correct, and could the witness repeat the third village.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- and the seat of this brigade was in Zenica, and they had to go through the area of responsibility of the 306th Mountain Brigade. So they did not have a seat in the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you repeat for the record the locations where the 314th Brigade was located, please, in the Bila Valley?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 314th Brigade was not in the Bila Valley, in that sense. The locals from the villages, Gluha Bukovica, Zagradje, Skomorje, with the already mentioned Hadzija Puric went and joined the 314th Brigade. They were born in those villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could you spell those names? I realise the transcript is having difficulty trying to get those names. Gluha Bukovica, is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: G-L-U-H-A, B-U-K-O-V-I-C-A; Z-A-G-R-A-D-J-E; and S-K-O-M-O-R-J-E.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And then you referred to Midhat Puric. Is it correct that he was in the 4th Battalion of the 314th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in which battalion he was, but it is correct that he was in the 314th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know when he joined that brigade?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He joined the brigade immediately after -- following the new year day between 1992 and 1993, at the time when we were establishing the 306th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And is it correct that later on he moved to the 27th Mountain Brigade of the 7th Corps of the ARBiH to become an administrative officer for information, propaganda, and education?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's impossible. I don't know what you mean, but I know this man. I absolutely don't know what you're talking about. I don't know where he was up to the end of the war, but it's impossible that he was an officer of such an --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe for clarification, Exhibit -- sorry, document D974 can be shown. This is a decision on commissions and promotions, while it's being presented, from the 4th of November, 1994. You can see the first page here for a second, and then I wish that we go to the fourth page, please, in English, and in B/C/S to page 3. In the English, it's the fourth person from the top; and in B/C/S it's somewhere in the middle, above the letter "E."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Something like the 10th person above the letter is "Midhat Puric." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- oh, yes, I see it now. I don't know if there's another person with the same name. However, this is the 7th Corps. I was never there, and I cannot know who was performing which duty or anything like that. But it would be quite incredible for me that Midhat Puric, called "Hadzija," would be carrying out such a duty, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was this father's name Zaim?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Although he lives in the neighbouring village, I don't know who his father is or his father's name.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: May the document be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is marked for identification. May it be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document will become Exhibit 1206, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I understood your testimony to say that at some point in time, in 1993, the Mujahedin formed their own unit. Could you tell me when the unit El Mudjahedin Detachment was approximately formed?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will be hard for me to remember the date or the time. It's sometime towards the end or the late second half of 1993, if I recall correctly, or maybe it's much later. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And can you tell me, the El Mujahid Detachment had no fixed area of responsibility within the Bila Valley; is that right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The El Mudjahedin Detachment, after it was formed, was not in the Bila Valley at all. It didn't have an area of responsibility; and very soon after it was established, it was relocated, with the exception of individuals who were individually living in the Bila Valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What about the village of Orasac, were there some members of the El Mujahedin living?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a much later period, after I went to the 3rd Corps, and all that was happening in the Bila Valley is something I don't know. But as for and Orasac, Guca Gora, and some other locations, we already mentioned Poljanice, a few Arabs were settled there. They were living there. As for which units they belonged to or what they were a part of, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me, the Mujahedin in Mehurici, they were engaging in combat; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about. Which Mujahedin from Mehurici and which fighting, which combat?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry. I meant the Mujahedin who moved from Mehurici to Poljanice. I apologise. So the Mujahedin who were based in Poljanice, did they engage in combat in 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We talked in detail about that yesterday. They did undertake some actions independently, but neither were they a unit, nor did they participate in combat with the 306th Mountain Brigade, and even frequently in danger of us clashing with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wasn't asking for the 306th Brigade and the relationship of the Mujahedin to it. Could you tell me - you're saying that the Mujahedin from Poljanice did some actions independently - where did they carry out these actions independently?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not a unit; and among other things, they tried to attack the feature that we talked about yesterday. This is the central feature in the middle of the Bila Valley called "Hrasce 688."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This was in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the date. It wasn't a large action that we would necessarily register in that way, but I know about it because they were attacked from there, so they were also responding or retaliating and attacking back.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you say they were attacked from there, do you wish to say that they were holding a part of the front line where they were attacked?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, absolutely no. Yesterday, we talked about how this was a feature from which all the roads in the Bila Valley were being controlled --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand that, but I'm just trying to follow up on what you said. You said, a moment ago, "They were attacked from there." So where were the Mujahedin located when they were attacked from Hrasce?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were attacked as they were moving along the Mehurici-Han Bila road.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know how many Mujahedin were moving along that road?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How would I be able to know that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we have document PT1555 shown to the witness. This is referring to another incident, a document from the 21st of September, 1993, entitled: "Information on the situation in the AOR of the 3rd Corps." If we could for a moment go to the last page and look for the signature, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we now go back to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is the fourth sentence of your report I'm referring to here: "After the Ustasha [indiscernible]," it starts, and I read it to you: "In Grbavica, Sivrino Selo was supposed to share the same fate as the Ahmici. Luckily, the Ustasha did not succeed in that, the 27th Krajiska Brigade intervened in time and taught them a lesson, so that Sivrino Selo was saved, and then the 17th Famous Krajiska Brigade from the direction of Kruscica, together with the El Mujahid Detachment, advanced to Princip. The village of Gacice burnt down completely. From the direction of Krcevine, the 7th Muslim Brigade pushed forward and slowly but gradually advanced below Lubice with the intention to link up with the soldiers of the Krajiska Brigade and to cut the communication towards Busovaca." Can you tell me, from your reporting here, where is Sivrino Selo and where is Kruscica located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sivrino Selo is in the area between Zenica and Vitez, thus in the area of the Vitez Municipality. Kruscica is located between Vitez and Novi Travnik, and I'm not sure whether it's in the Novi Travnik Municipality or the Vitez Municipality. With that, this document went out as information to the subordinate unit. I think you can see from the contents that it was drafted on the basis of information from the media, and I'm trying to inform the fighters who don't have radios, who are in Vlasic Mountain. Well, it's not an official document that's going anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell me whether the two locations, Krus cica and Sivrino Selo, are not within the 306th Mountain Brigade controlled territory, they are outside the territory held by the 306th Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were very far from the territory controlled by the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: How could you obtain that information?

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that this was information that we got from the media, because at the Commands, we were able to listen to the news and the propaganda. So we would assemble this information and forward it to the fighters who were on combat positions at Mount Vlasic and who did not have the option or the possibility of communication or listening to the media.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me understand you, sir. Are you saying you were feeding your subordinates propaganda instead of giving them factual information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. We --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You collect information from the radio which you call propaganda, and you pass it on to your subordinates, to your units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Information from the radio, we would write them down and forward that to our subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me quote what you said just now, at line 21 of page 85: "I just said that this was information that we got from the media, because at the Commands, we were able to listen to the news and the propaganda. So we would assemble this information and forward it to the fighters who were on combat positions on Mount Vlasic and who did not have the option or possibility of communication or listening to the media." Now, you're collecting information from the radio, including propaganda, and you pass it on to your units. This is what you were doing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We sent information from the media to our units. What was the truth and what was propaganda is something that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't agree that the witness mentioned the word "propaganda" at all in his answer in this context, and now he has clarified it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It would have been preferable, Madam Vidovic, if you had objected at the time he was being translated, and you would have told us that the witness did not use the word "propaganda." To raise it at this stage, when he is now being confront with this question, is of no value. You may proceed. I am done with my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I note the time. I would have one more question, and then would ask for the document be admitted, if this is permitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We can see here that you're using the term "El Mudjahedin Detachment," and we see the document has a stamp from the 21st of September [Realtime transcript read in error "December"] 1993. Can I assume that, by that time, the El Mudjahedin Detachment was established? Sorry. I was referring to 21 "September" 1993. The transcript says "December."

utterances.speaker: HALIM HUSIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've seen that this term "El Mujahid" functions - or the Mujahedin - already from 1992, so I'm not sure whether it was formed before or after this date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. Excuse me. Witness, please, in 1992, we had the word "Mujahedin" and "Mujahid," or "El Mudjahedin Detachment." Did we have the word "Mujahid" or did we have "El Mudjahedin Detachment"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The official name of the detachment, after it was established, was "El Mujahedin." But much earlier, before it was formed, there was a large number of different terms which were used for the same group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but this is not what I asked. Please, let me give you the context. The Prosecutor asked you whether at that time, at that very date in September 1993, the El Mujahid or El Mujahedin, or whatever detachment, had already been established, given that in this document, which dates back to September 1993, there is a reference - you actually refer to this, to these words, and you answered by saying, "Well, this word 'Mujahid,' 'Mujahedin' had already been used as early as 1992. I just wanted to know whether, in 1992, the words "El Mudjahedin Detachment" was used.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May this document please be given an exhibit number. It has been admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document will become Exhibit 1207.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That brings us to the end of today's session, sir. We are still not done with you. You will please have to come back tomorrow. Let's just adjourn while you are here so that you know the time. The Court adjourns to tomorrow morning at 9.00 in Courtroom I. I guess everybody agreed to that change. Okay. 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I, sir. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 13th day of March, 2008, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.07 p.m.,
